summary: No relevant testing skill found. Verified the exact legacy qr/no-reason flow end to end: a qr session with phone set and no last_disconnect_label now shows the 'Why did this drop?' fallback banner with 'Reason not recorded for this drop.' and all 3 common causes. Verified recorded-label QR UI, disconnect history empty and ordered states, and status metadata. Connected-session no-banner check was verified with a MOCKED status response because no real connected WhatsApp account is available in preview.

minor.issue: When called with code=440 but without a label, the backend stores last_disconnect_label as 'Code 440' instead of deriving the friendly 'Replaced by another device...' label. The normal Node pipeline sends labelForCode(code), so the user-facing flow still passed, but the endpoint is less robust than the test note implied.

action_items: Optional hardening: make /api/internal/disconnect-event derive known labels from code when payload.label is omitted, so direct code=440 test calls also get the friendly reason.
critical_code_review_comments: SessionDetail.jsx renders data-testid=disconnect-reason for all !isConnected states; this fixes the reported legacy QR/no-label silence. It may be broader than the stated 'previously linked' condition for brand-new not-connected sessions, but that was not observed as a blocker for the reported bug.
GET /api/sessions/{id}/status returned error, error_code, error_label, last_disconnect_at, last_disconnect_code, last_disconnect_label, and last_disconnect_terminal after a recorded disconnect event.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for real QR/history UI checks; connected no-banner was MOCKED

context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/test_reports/disconnect_reason_backend_results.json for the seeded session IDs. UI automation passed against the preview URL; connected-state check was MOCKED only due lack of a real connected WhatsApp session.
rca_of_the_issue: Original issue reproduced as the legacy data shape: status=qr, phone set, no error_label/last_disconnect_label. After the fix, SessionDetail still renders the reason banner and falls back to common causes, so the customer now gets an explanation instead of silence.
